title: How do I measure the performance of my direct mail campaigns?
summary: Here’s how to measure response, conversion, attribution, and delivery to prove direct mail campaign performance.
body_markdown:
Just like all of your[other marketing channels](https://www.lob.com/blog/how-can-i-integrate-direct-mail-campaigns-with-my-existing-digital-marketing-tools) , you need to be able to track the success of your direct mail program. But how do you measure a physical medium? Here are some KPIs worth tracking and how to connect them to outcomes.


## Delivery and in-home rate


Most metrics depend on knowing how many pieces actually reached recipients.[Delivery rate](https://www.lob.com/blog/what-do-usps-tracking-scan-events-actually-mean) tracks what percentage of mail landed. In-home rate tracks when it arrived. Both matter for timing follow-up across other channels and for making sure you’re measuring against an accurate baseline.


## Response rate


Response rate measures how many recipients take *any* action after receiving your mail – visiting a website, calling a number, scanning a QR code, or filling out a form. It’s the direct mail equivalent of digital click-through rate.


## Conversion rate


How many recipients followed through on your target action? High response but low conversion usually means the mail got your audience’s attention, but the next step didn’t close the deal. Make sure your web or in-store experience delivers on the promise or offer in your mailpiece.


## ‍ **Direct and indirect attribution**


There are two ways to measure direct mail: directly and indirectly. While QR code scans and visits to pURLs can be directly tracked, other types of actions are tougher to nail down.


## Match-back analysis


Not every response comes through a trackable mechanism. Some recipients convert by searching your brand online or walking into a store. Match-back analysis compares your mailing list against customer transaction records to attribute purchases to campaigns within a defined window, even without a code or QR scan.


## Start with your own baseline


Industry benchmarks give you context, but[your own campaign history](https://www.lob.com/category/direct-mail-q-as#:~:text=How%20do%20you%20run%20an%20A/B%20test%20in%20direct%20mail%3F) is the most useful reference. Use early campaigns to establish a baseline, then focus on improving it through better lists, stronger offers, and smarter timing.
